deficiencies.description: The rewrite changes the grammatical and conceptual role of “maturation”. In the source, maturation is a context during which the ongoing development or differentiation occurs; in the rewrite, maturation itself becomes a process said to occur from infancy to adulthood.
deficiencies.sourcePassage: And not to say that all of it does, because obviously during adolescence and maturation, this occurs from infancy to adulthood.
deficiencies.rewritePassage: This is not to say that all of it does, because differentiation and maturation also occur from infancy to adulthood.

deficiencies.description: The source phrase is incomplete or ambiguous as to whether signalling and providing a basis for adherence are separate functions. The rewrite resolves it as the single concept “a signalling basis”, choosing an interpretation that the source does not clearly establish.
deficiencies.sourcePassage: It gives them structure and provides a signaling and basis for their adherence to this layer.
deficiencies.rewritePassage: It gives them structure and provides a signalling basis for their adherence to this layer.

deficiencies.description: The rewrite changes “invading stroma” to “invaded stroma”, thereby changing the role or state attributed to the stroma.
deficiencies.sourcePassage: So the invasion that we're talking about is to get those, if you like, those deranged cells to go from this morphology past the basement membrane, which would be here into the invading stroma.
deficiencies.rewritePassage: The invasion under discussion is the process by which these deranged cells go from this morphology past the basement membrane into the invaded stroma.

considerations.sourcePassage: So we've all, everybody sitting in this room, has executed a fantastic differentiation program that has started when you were a zygote, you were just a single cell.
considerations.reason: The rewrite preserves the claim that differentiation begins with the single-cell zygote; replacing audience-directed wording and “fantastic” with general textbook prose is stylistic.

considerations.sourcePassage: And obviously, you've executed this program of differentiation during embryogenesis and growth in the womb.
considerations.reason: The rewrite states the same timing and context for the differentiation programme.

considerations.sourcePassage: Here at this stage here, most of your growth, really, most of your lineage specification and your expansive growth has happened during embryogenesis, during the time that you were born.
considerations.reason: The rewrite retains the substantive point about lineage specification and expansive growth during embryogenesis. The final temporal phrase in the source is a disfluent restatement and does not establish a distinct clear fact.

considerations.sourcePassage: Because if you think you go from a totipotent single cell to having all these different cell lineages and this expansive growth, a lot of your development and differentiation occurs obviously in the womb.
considerations.reason: The rewrite faithfully preserves the transition from a totipotent cell to multiple lineages and the occurrence of substantial development and differentiation in the womb.

considerations.sourcePassage: So there's this very elaborate and sophisticated program of differentiation that occurs, and every cell in the body understands its, if you like, its program and its differentiation.
considerations.reason: The rewrite retains both the sophisticated differentiation programme and the claim that each cell follows its own programme.

considerations.sourcePassage: So we are composed of many organs. Organs are composed of tissues, tissues are composed of cells, and tissues are extremely complex in that these cells are constantly turning over, and they all participate in a community to make that tissue functional.
considerations.reason: The rewrite preserves the anatomical hierarchy, cellular turnover and cooperative contribution to tissue function.

considerations.sourcePassage: So if you just look here at this little section of skin, skin has a number of functions, everything from barrier functions to immune functions to sensory functions to temperature regulation. It's doing a lot of things, and many different cell types in the skin participate in that function. So you can see them all just listed here, all working together to make the skin work.
considerations.reason: All four stated skin functions and the cooperation of multiple cell types are retained; audience-directed and repetitive wording is appropriately removed.

considerations.sourcePassage: And there's also inherent in the skin a program of repair and regeneration because skin is obviously always turning over as well. So there's a very strong developmental program for every cell to understand and know what it's doing and also what it's doing in relation to its neighbors.
considerations.reason: The rewrite retains the repair and regeneration programme, its relationship to turnover, and each cell's relation to neighbouring cells.

considerations.sourcePassage: Well, cancer, you have to think, is therefore a failure of this program, a failure of the cell, a single cell, to understand its role in this bigger picture of a tissue.
considerations.reason: The definition of cancer as failure of a single cell to follow its role within a tissue is preserved.

considerations.sourcePassage: So there's a failure of this three-dimensional growth program, which leads to the growth of a tumor within in situ, within a, if you like, a single space. But then gradually over time, this tumor will, or cells within the tumor will gain the capacity to move around the body, to invade and metastasize throughout the body.
considerations.reason: The rewrite retains the failure of three-dimensional growth, in-situ tumour growth, and the later acquisition of invasion and metastatic capacity. British spellings are allowed.

considerations.sourcePassage: And because our understanding of three-dimensional growth and tissue architecture is limited, it is harder for us to kind of understand what exactly is going wrong, what signals does the cell-- what signals become aberrant within the cell to enable this failure of differentiation.
considerations.reason: The rewrite preserves the causal link between limited understanding and difficulty identifying the aberrant intracellular signals; the false start is appropriately removed.

considerations.sourcePassage: So over years and centuries, we've been using a lot of different tools to try and understand this biology. So histology being one of them, of course.
considerations.reason: The rewrite retains the long-term use of multiple tools and identifies histology as one of them.

considerations.sourcePassage: So if you take a tissue section, this is of a normal breast tissue, and you look at the histology, you will see that the tissue is incredibly well-organized, even at this scale. So you can see here is a normal milk duct. You'll see that the epithelial cells here are arranged. They look fairly uniform in shape and size.
considerations.reason: The rewrite retains the observations that normal breast tissue is well organised and that the epithelial cells of the normal milk duct are uniformly arranged in shape and size.

considerations.sourcePassage: They have the nucleus on the layer towards the lumen, so they're apical basal regulation in terms of the orientation of those cells within the tissue.
considerations.reason: Despite the source's grammatical disfluency, it links the luminal nuclear position with apical-basal regulation; the rewrite preserves that intended link without adding a different scientific claim.

considerations.sourcePassage: And you'll see that the stroma is very well behaved. You have vessels here, and you have fibroblasts sitting within the stroma.
considerations.reason: The rewrite retains the description of the stroma and the presence of vessels and fibroblasts.

considerations.sourcePassage: So what we need to understand is how does a cell here go from obeying its program, moving into this kind of configuration where the cell is growing into the stroma, and also in this kind of deranged manner.
considerations.reason: The rewrite preserves the question of how a cell changes from obeying its programme to deranged growth into the stroma.

considerations.sourcePassage: And you can see here now the cells are all of different shapes and sizes. They have come in, they have lost this architecture, moved over the basement membrane and invaded and are growing within the stroma.
considerations.reason: The rewrite retains the variation in cell shape and size, loss of architecture, passage over the basement membrane, invasion and growth within the stroma. The vague phrase “have come in” adds no separate clear observation.

considerations.sourcePassage: Right? So what has happened to lose the structure and to get this invasion?
considerations.reason: The rewrite preserves the question about what caused the loss of structure and invasion.

considerations.sourcePassage: And so again, what I want you to appreciate, although it's extremely hard to see by histology, is the fact that these epithelial cells have invaded into the stroma, so they have crossed a basement membrane. It's very hard to see.
considerations.reason: The rewrite retains the invasion into the stroma, crossing of the basement membrane and difficulty of seeing this by histology.

considerations.sourcePassage: So I've actually given you three pictures of it here for you to appreciate what this structure looks like in the context of epithelial cells.
considerations.reason: The rewrite retains the fact that three pictures show the basement membrane in the context of epithelial cells.

considerations.sourcePassage: So you'll see that it's a specialized extracellular matrix that the cells are sitting on.
considerations.reason: The rewrite faithfully identifies the basement membrane as a specialised extracellular matrix on which the cells sit.

considerations.sourcePassage: When you're looking within, for example, the intestines, you can see that this epithelial layer is very thin, only one cell thick. And here, the basement membrane protein here is red. So you can see that it stretches all the way along the inside of this finger-like villus projection.
considerations.reason: The rewrite retains the one-cell-thick intestinal epithelium, the red basement-membrane protein and its extent along the inside of the finger-like villus projection.
